GRAND RAPIDS FAMILY NETWORK

The city is part of your family support system.

Parent University connects GRPS families to trusted Grand Rapids and Kent County organizations for learning, health, housing, food, child care, activities, careers and more. Start with what you need—we will help narrow the options.

LEARNING

Grand Rapids Public Library

Homework tools, early literacy, teen resources, free events, digital books and GRPS Connect resources.

Explore GRPL + GRPS Connect ↗
FOOD & ESSENTIALS

Find food near you

Use local food pantry, mobile pantry and family resource tools instead of searching agency by agency.

MENTAL HEALTH

Help for children, teens & families

Network180, Arbor Circle and other local supports can help with counseling, crisis support and family navigation.

FREE & LOW-COST FUN

Explore Grand Rapids together

Parks, libraries, museums, recreation programs and youth activities can make learning and belonging part of everyday family life.

EARLY CHILDHOOD

Start strong from birth to PreK

Early On, free PreK, child care, developmental support and family coaching are available across Kent County.

HOUSING & LEGAL HELP

Get help when stability is at risk

Local housing, shelter, utility and free civil legal resources can help families address urgent barriers.

TEENS & FUTURE

Jobs, careers, training & college

Promise Zone, GRCC, Kent Career Tech Center, West Michigan Works! and local youth programs help scholars plan what comes next.

NEW TO GRAND RAPIDS

Find your way around a new community

Language, newcomer, education, employment, health and family supports are easier to navigate from one starting point.

BY AGE, STAGE & SUPPORT

ABOUT PARENT UNIVERSITY

Helping caregivers become confident partners and advocates.

Keep Parent University's history and purpose, but make the public experience concise, current and action-oriented.

OUR PURPOSE

Family learning + family support + family voice

Parent University is a community-centered way for caregivers to build knowledge, access support and participate fully in their scholar’s education.
